q: Pendulum C will oscillate with the greatest amplitude since its ____ matches that of pendulum A which provides the driving force.
e: Pendulum C will oscillate with the greatest amplitude since its natural frequency matches that of pendulum A which provides the driving force. Natural frequency is what this statement is using.

q: The amplitude of the motion reaches a maximum when the frequency of driving force equals the ____ of the system.
e: Frequency is the number of turns per second, the reciprocal of the period. The amplitude of the motion reaches a maximum when the frequency of driving force equals the natural frequency of the system.

q: Under this condition, the system is said to be in ____.
e: Under this condition, the system is said to be in resonance. Resonance is what this statement is using.

q: The frequency at which resonance occurs is called the ____ of the system.
e: Frequency is the number of turns per second, the reciprocal of the period. The frequency at which resonance occurs is called the resonant frequency of the system.

q: Natural frequency is the frequency at which a system tends to oscillate in the absence of any ____.
e: Frequency is the number of turns per second, the reciprocal of the period. Natural frequency is the frequency at which a system tends to oscillate in the absence of any driving force.

q: The resonant sound will be heard at certain different length of ____.
e: The resonant sound will be heard at certain different length of air column. Air column is what this statement is using.

q: A resonance column tube will have an ____ near the open end and a node at the water surface.
e: Standing waves stay put with nodes and antinodes. Progressive waves travel and carry energy. A resonance column tube will have an antinode near the open end and a node at the water surface.

q: At the closed end of a resonance column, a ____ will be formed because air molecules cannot move.
e: At the closed end of a resonance column, a node will be formed because air molecules cannot move. Node is what this statement is using.

q: Resonance can only be produced under the situation where a node is formed at the water surface and an ____ is formed at the open end.
e: Standing waves stay put with nodes and antinodes. Progressive waves travel and carry energy. Resonance can only be produced under the situation where a node is formed at the water surface and an antinode is formed at the open end.

q: Using the resonance equations, the wavelength of the vibrating air column is ____.
e: Using the resonance equations, the wavelength of the vibrating air column is λ = 2(l_2 - l_1). Leave the relation as λ = 2(l_2 - l_1).

q: At resonance, the velocity of sound can be found using the formula ____.
e: At resonance, the velocity of sound can be found using the formula v = fλ. Leave the relation as v = fλ.

q: In closed organ pipes, an antinode exists near the open end while a ____ is formed at the closed end.
e: Standing waves stay put with nodes and antinodes. Progressive waves travel and carry energy. In closed organ pipes, an antinode exists near the open end while a node is formed at the closed end.

q: The wavelength of the $n^{th}$ harmonic for a vibrating air column in a closed organ pipe is ____.
e: The wavelength of the n^th harmonic for a vibrating air column in a closed organ pipe is λ_n = (4l)/(n). Leave the relation as λ_n = (4l)/(n).

q: The frequency of a closed organ pipe is given by the formula ____.
e: Frequency is the number of turns per second, the reciprocal of the period. The frequency of a closed organ pipe is given by the formula f_n = (nv)/(4l).

q: A closed organ pipe produces only ____ harmonics.
e: Harmonics are integer multiples of the fundamental frequency. A closed organ pipe produces only odd harmonics.

q: In a closed organ pipe, the third harmonic is called the first ____.
e: In a closed organ pipe, the third harmonic is called the first overtone. The name used here is overtone.

q: The stationary wave with a single node in the open organ pipe corresponds to ____ (first harmonic).
e: Standing waves stay put with nodes and antinodes. Progressive waves travel and carry energy. The stationary wave with a single node in the open organ pipe corresponds to fundamental frequency (first harmonic).

q: The wavelength for the $n^{th}$ harmonic in an open organ pipe is ____.
e: The wavelength for the n^th harmonic in an open organ pipe is λ_n = (2l)/(n). Leave the relation as λ_n = (2l)/(n).

q: The frequencies of a vibrating air column in an open organ pipe are given by ____.
e: The frequencies of a vibrating air column in an open organ pipe are given by f_n = (nv)/(2l). Leave the relation as f_n = (nv)/(2l).

q: A flute can be modeled as a pipe open at both ends, while a clarinet can be modeled as a pipe ____ at one end.
e: A flute can be modeled as a pipe open at both ends, while a clarinet can be modeled as a pipe closed at one end. Closed is what this statement is using.

q: Beats are the periodic fluctuation heard in the ____ of sound when two sound waves of slightly different frequencies interfere with one another.
e: Lenses refract. Light is an electromagnetic wave and also a particle. Beats are the periodic fluctuation heard in the intensity of sound when two sound waves of slightly different frequencies interfere with one another.

q: The number of beats per second, or beat frequency, is the ____ in frequency between the two sources.
e: Frequency is the number of turns per second, the reciprocal of the period. The number of beats per second, or beat frequency, is the difference in frequency between the two sources.

q: The beat frequency is calculated using the formula ____.
e: Frequency is the number of turns per second, the reciprocal of the period. The beat frequency is calculated using the formula f_b = |f_1 - f_2|.
